heading.en: If light can be a particle, can an electron be a wave?

hook.en: De Broglie asked this question in 1924. The answer is yes, and it is why electron microscopes can see far finer detail than light microscopes.
hook.kn: 1924 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಡಿ ಬ್ರೋಗ್ಲಿ ಈ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಕೇಳಿದರು. ಉತ್ತರ ಹೌದು; ಅದಕ್ಕಾಗಿಯೇ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕಗಳು ಬೆಳಕಿನ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮ ವಿವರ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: Find the wavelength of electrons accelerated through V
Explain why everyday objects show no wave behaviour

say.en: De Broglie asked this question in 1924. The answer is yes, and it is why electron microscopes can see far finer detail than light microscopes. In this lesson: State the de Broglie relation.
Find the wavelength of electrons accelerated through V.
Explain why everyday objects show no wave behaviour.

body.en: A particle of momentum $p$ has an associated wavelength $\lambda = h/p = h/mv$. In terms of kinetic energy, $\lambda = h/\sqrt{2mK}$. For a charge $q$ accelerated from rest through potential $V$, $K = qV$, so $\lambda = h/\sqrt{2mqV}$. For an electron this gives $\lambda = 1.227/\sqrt{V}$ nm.
body.kn: p ಸಂವೇಗದ ಕಣಕ್ಕೆ λ = h/p ತರಂಗಾಂತರ ಇದೆ. λ = h/√(2mK). V ವಿಭವದ ಮೂಲಕ ವೇಗವರ್ಧಿತ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗೆ λ = 1.227/√V nm.

narration.en: Let us find the wavelength of moving particles, from electrons to cricket balls.

say.en: de Broglie proposed that every moving particle has a wavelength h over its momentum.
An electron accelerated through V volts has kinetic energy eV, so its momentum is root 2 m e V. That gives λ = 1.227 over root V nanometres.
At 100 volts, λ is about 0.123 nanometres, the same size as X-ray wavelengths. That is why electrons diffract from crystals.
A 0.1 kg ball at 10 m/s has a wavelength of about 10⁻³³ m, far too small to detect.
For electrons, λ falls as one over the square root of the accelerating voltage.

title.en: Why we do not notice matter waves

body.en: For a cricket ball the de Broglie wavelength is about $10^{-34}$ m, far smaller than any slit or atom, so no diffraction can be seen. For electrons accelerated through a few hundred volts, $\lambda$ is about $0.1$ nm, comparable to the spacing of atoms in a crystal, so their *wave nature* shows up. Lighter and slower particles have longer wavelengths.
body.kn: ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್ ಚೆಂಡಿನ ತರಂಗಾಂತರ ಸುಮಾರು 10⁻³⁴ m, ಕಾಣಲು ಅತಿ ಚಿಕ್ಕದು. ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳ ತರಂಗಾಂತರ ಸುಮಾರು 0.1 nm, ಸ್ಫಟಿಕದ ಪರಮಾಣು ಅಂತರಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮ.

lambda equals 1.227/ the square root of V nm.
lambda equals 1.227/ the square root of 100 equals 0.1227 nanometres.
So the answer is is approximately 0.123 nanometres.

problem.en: Find the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.12 kg ball moving at 20 m/s.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.12 kg ball moving at 20 m/s.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.12 kilograms ball moving at 20 metres per second.
p equals mv equals 0.12 times 20 equals 2.4 kilograms metres per second.
lambda equals h over p equals 6.63 times 10 to the power minus 34 over 2.4 is approximately 2.8 times 10 to the power minus 34 metres.
So the answer is is approximately 2.8 times 10 to the power minus 34 metres.
